definition: to enjoy something very much or look forward to it with pleasure

examples.text: The old sailor relishes the telling of every storm he survived.
The general relished the chance to face his old rival in the field.
I relish the first cold morning of autumn.

confused.note: To relish is to enjoy greatly; to relinquish is to give up.

questions.passage: Most performers dread hostile audiences. The comedian, by contrast, seemed to ______ them, saving her sharpest jokes for the moments when someone in the crowd shouted an insult.
questions.explanation: Saving her best material for hecklers shows she enjoyed the challenge.

distractors.why: Negate means to cancel out, which does not fit.
Allocate means to distribute for a purpose, which does not fit.
Surmise means to guess, which does not capture her enjoyment.

definition: to give a share of something to someone or for a particular purpose

examples.text: The council allocated one tenth of the harvest to feed the army.
The grant allocates funds for three years of fieldwork.
I allocate two hours on Sunday to planning the week.

confused.note: To allocate is to set aside for a purpose; to locate is to find.

questions.passage: With only forty hours of telescope time available, the committee had to decide how to ______ them. It gave half to the search for distant galaxies and divided the rest among six smaller projects.
questions.explanation: Dividing the hours among projects is distributing them for particular purposes.

distractors.why: Renovate means to restore to good condition, which does not fit hours.
Implicate means to show involvement in wrongdoing, which does not fit.
Evoke means to call up a feeling, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin locus, "place": to place toward

definition: active at night; happening at night

examples.text: Owls are nocturnal hunters with eyes adapted to dim light.
The poet takes long nocturnal walks through the sleeping city.
My hamster is nocturnal, which is why the wheel squeaks at two in the morning.

confused.note: Nocturnal means active at night; diurnal means active by day.

questions.passage: Because the desert is dangerously hot by day, most of its animals are ______. They spend the daylight hours in burrows and emerge to feed only after the sun has set.
questions.explanation: Animals that come out only after sunset are active at night.

distractors.why: Formidable means impressively powerful, which does not describe when animals are active.
Salutary means beneficial, which does not fit.
Chronological means arranged in order of time, which does not fit.

definition: an event that causes great damage or suffering; a disaster

examples.text: The flood of 1931 was the worst calamity in the province's history.
One calamity follows another until the heroine has lost everything but her wit.
Dropping the cake on the way to the party felt like a calamity at the time.

confused.note: A calamity is a disaster; calumny is a false statement that damages a reputation.

questions.passage: The failure of the wheat harvest was a ______ for the region. With no grain to sell and little to eat, thousands of families abandoned their farms and walked to the cities in search of work.
questions.explanation: A failed harvest that drives thousands from their homes is a disaster.

distractors.why: A prerogative is a special right, which does not fit.
A skirmish is a minor fight, which does not describe a failed harvest.
An aptitude is a natural ability, which does not fit.

definition: to repair and improve something old, especially a building

examples.text: The duke renovated the ruined castle and made it his summer home.
The observatory was renovated to house a larger telescope.
My parents spent a year renovating the kitchen themselves.

confused.note: To renovate is to restore something old; to innovate is to introduce something new.

questions.passage: The city chose not to tear down the old train station. It decided instead to ______ the building, replacing the roof, restoring the tiled floors, and converting the waiting hall into a public market.
questions.explanation: Repairing and restoring an old building is renovating it.

distractors.why: Negate means to cancel out, which does not fit a building.
Antagonize means to provoke hostility, which does not fit.
Oscillate means to swing back and forth, which does not fit.

definition: to cause something to have no effect; to cancel out

examples.text: The second drug negated the benefits of the first.
The new treaty negated every promise made in the old one.
Eating three cookies after my run negated the workout.

confused.note: To negate is to cancel out; to neglect is to fail to care for.

questions.passage: The new engine uses a tenth less fuel than the old one. That saving is largely ______, however, by the weight of the larger battery the engine requires.
questions.explanation: The extra weight cancels out the fuel saving.

distractors.why: Proliferated means multiplied rapidly, which does not fit.
Attested means confirmed as true, the opposite of cancelling.
Renovated means restored, which does not fit.

definition: to show that someone is involved in a crime or something bad

examples.text: Letters found in his desk implicated the minister in the plot.
Recent studies implicate the gene in several inherited diseases.
The chocolate on my brother's face implicated him in the case of the missing cake.

confused.note: To implicate is to show involvement in wrongdoing; to imply is to suggest without saying.

questions.passage: The clerk insisted that he had acted alone. Bank records, however, ______ two of his supervisors, who had approved each of the false payments and received a share of the money.
questions.explanation: Records showing the supervisors approved and profited tie them to the crime.

distractors.why: Exonerated means cleared of blame, the opposite of what the records did.
Allocated means distributed, which does not fit.
Relished means enjoyed, which does not fit.

definition: to increase rapidly in number or amount

examples.text: Bacteria proliferate quickly in warm, moist conditions.
Printing shops proliferated across Europe within fifty years of the first press.
Coffee shops have proliferated on our street; there are now five.

confused.note: To proliferate is to multiply; to prolong is to make last longer.

questions.passage: In 1990 the city had three farmers' markets. Since then they have ______: there are now more than sixty, and nearly every neighborhood has one within walking distance.
questions.explanation: Growing from three to more than sixty is a rapid increase in number.

distractors.why: Languished means weakened or been neglected, the opposite of multiplying.
Oscillated means swung back and forth, which does not describe steady growth.
Convened means gathered for a meeting, which does not fit.

definition: to keep moving or changing between two positions, states, or opinions

examples.text: The pendulum oscillates with a period of exactly two seconds.
Public opinion oscillated between war and peace throughout the summer.
My mood oscillates between excitement and panic as the trip gets closer.

confused.note: To oscillate is to swing back and forth; to osculate is a formal word for to kiss.

questions.passage: The country's policy toward its neighbor has never been consistent. For decades it has ______ between friendship and hostility, signing a trade agreement in one year and closing the border in the next.
questions.explanation: Moving back and forth between two stances is oscillating.

distractors.why: Proliferated means multiplied, which does not fit.
Flourished means thrived, which does not describe a shifting policy.
Prevailed means won out, which does not fit.

definition: having a good effect, especially after something unpleasant

examples.text: The defeat had a salutary effect on the army's overconfident officers.
A week of rest had a salutary effect on the patient's blood pressure.
Failing the first quiz was a salutary shock that got me studying.

confused.note: Salutary means beneficial; solitary means alone.

questions.passage: Losing the opening match by five goals was painful, but the coach called it a ______ lesson. The players stopped assuming they would win, trained harder, and did not lose again that season.
questions.explanation: A painful loss that led to improvement had a good effect.

distractors.why: Formidable means impressively powerful, which does not describe a lesson with good effects.
Harrowing means extremely distressing; the coach stresses the benefit, not the pain.
Nocturnal means active at night, which does not fit.

definition: impressive and powerful in a way that causes fear or respect

examples.text: The fortress on the cliff was a formidable obstacle to any invader.
Decoding the genome was a formidable task.
My grandmother is a formidable chess player who shows no mercy.

confused.note: Formidable means inspiring fear or respect; formative means shaping development.

questions.passage: The young lawyer knew she faced a ______ opponent. Her rival had not lost a case in twelve years and was famous for dismantling witnesses with a few quiet questions.
questions.explanation: An opponent with such a record inspires fear and respect.

distractors.why: Insightful means perceptive; the details stress how hard he is to beat.
Convivial means friendly and festive, which does not fit.
Salutary means beneficial, which does not describe an opponent.

definition: a system of government or management with many complicated rules and officials

examples.text: The empire's vast bureaucracy kept records of every bushel of grain.
Researchers complained that bureaucracy delayed the permits by two years.
Replacing a lost student ID involves a surprising amount of bureaucracy.

confused.note: A bureaucracy is rule by officials and procedures; a democracy is rule by the people.

questions.passage: Opening a small shop in the city once required patience. An applicant had to visit eleven offices, fill out forty forms, and wait as long as two years, a degree of ______ that drove many to give up.
questions.explanation: Eleven offices and forty forms are complicated official procedure.

distractors.why: Notoriety is fame for something bad, which does not fit.
Parity is equality, which does not fit.
Aptitude is natural ability, which does not fit.

definition: arranged in the order in which events happened

examples.text: The exhibit presents the letters in chronological order, from 1840 to 1865.
The novel abandons chronological order and begins with its ending.
My photos are in chronological order, so the haircut disaster is easy to find.

confused.note: Chronological means in order of time; chronic means lasting a long time.

questions.passage: The biography does not follow a ______ plan. It opens with the scientist's death, moves backward to her greatest discovery, and reaches her childhood only in the final chapter.
questions.explanation: A book that does not proceed from earliest to latest is not in time order.

distractors.why: Insightful means perceptive, which is not what the description of the book's order shows.
Nocturnal means active at night, which does not fit.
Secular means not religious, which does not fit.

definition: a natural ability to do something well or to learn it quickly

examples.text: The young apprentice showed a remarkable aptitude for mapmaking.
The test measures aptitude for spatial reasoning.
My sister has an aptitude for languages; I have an aptitude for naps.

confused.note: Aptitude is natural ability; attitude is a way of thinking or feeling.

questions.passage: The boy had never taken a music lesson. His ______ was obvious, however, when he sat down at a piano for the first time and picked out, by ear, a tune he had heard once on the radio.
questions.explanation: Playing by ear with no training shows natural ability.

distractors.why: A prerogative is a special right, not a talent.
Notoriety is fame for something bad, which does not fit.
A connotation is an implied meaning of a word, which does not fit.

definition: a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause

examples.text: An anonymous benefactor paid for the town's first hospital.
The orphan's mysterious benefactor turns out to be the convict he once helped.
The team's benefactor is a local baker who supplies free bread after every game.

confused.note: A benefactor gives help; a beneficiary receives it.

questions.passage: The orchestra would have closed years ago without its ______. A retired engineer who loved music, she covered its losses every season and asked only that her name never be printed in the program.
questions.explanation: Someone who covers the orchestra's losses gives it money and help.

distractors.why: A beneficiary receives help; she is the one giving it.
A demagogue is a leader who stirs up emotions, which does not fit.
A predecessor is someone who held a position earlier, which does not fit.

definition: a right or privilege that belongs to a particular person or group

examples.text: Declaring war was the prerogative of the king alone.
It is a grandmother's prerogative to spoil the children.
Choosing the music is the driver's prerogative.

confused.note: A prerogative is a right; a perquisite (perk) is an extra benefit that comes with a job.

questions.passage: Under the old constitution, choosing the judges was the ______ of the president alone. A reform passed in 1994 required that each appointment also be approved by the senate.
questions.explanation: A power belonging to the president alone is an exclusive right.

distractors.why: A calamity is a disaster, which does not fit.
A connotation is an implied meaning, which does not fit.
A skirmish is a minor fight, which does not fit.

definition: a short fight or argument that is not part of a major battle

examples.text: A skirmish at the river crossing delayed the army by a day.
The sisters' daily skirmishes over the mirror amuse their father.
There was a brief skirmish over the remote before the movie started.

confused.note: A skirmish is a small fight; a scrimmage is a practice game.

questions.passage: Historians once described the encounter as a great battle. Recent research suggests it was no more than a ______, a brief exchange between two scouting parties that left only a handful of casualties.
questions.explanation: A brief exchange between scouting parties is a minor fight.

distractors.why: A calamity is a great disaster, too strong for a minor exchange.
A bureaucracy is a system of officials, which does not fit.
A prerogative is a right, which does not fit.

definition: to guess that something is true without having proof

examples.text: From the mud on his boots, the detective surmises that the visitor walked from the station.
Scholars surmise that the scroll was copied by a single scribe.
I surmised from the smell that someone had burned the toast.

confused.note: To surmise is to guess; to summarize is to give the main points.

questions.passage: No record states why the settlement was abandoned. Archaeologists ______, from the absence of weapons and the orderly way tools were stored, that the inhabitants left peacefully and expected to return.
questions.explanation: Drawing a conclusion without direct proof is making an informed guess.

distractors.why: Attest means to confirm as true; without records they can only guess.
Antagonize means to provoke hostility, which does not fit.
Allocate means to distribute, which does not fit.

definition: to make someone feel hostile or angry toward you

examples.text: The new tax antagonized the very merchants the king most needed.
She cannot resist antagonizing her pompous cousin at every dinner.
Do not antagonize the cat; she remembers everything.

confused.note: To antagonize is to provoke hostility; to agonize is to worry intensely.

questions.passage: The new director's first speech managed to ______ nearly everyone in the room. She described the staff as "comfortable," their methods as "quaint," and their most successful product as "a happy accident."
questions.explanation: Insulting the staff and their work made them hostile.

distractors.why: Placate means to calm, the opposite of what her remarks did.
Renovate means to restore, which does not fit.
Evoke means to call up a feeling or memory; she provoked the people themselves.

partsNote: from Greek agon, "contest": to struggle against

definition: to become weak or fail to make progress; to remain in an unpleasant situation

examples.text: The explorer languished in prison for six years before his pardon.
Without sunlight the seedlings languished and turned pale.
My application has languished in someone's inbox for a month.

confused.note: Languish is a verb meaning to weaken or be neglected; languid is an adjective meaning slow and relaxed.

questions.passage: The proposal to build a new bridge was approved in 1998. It then ______ for twenty years, passed from committee to committee, while the old bridge grew steadily more dangerous.
questions.explanation: A plan left without progress for twenty years was neglected and stalled.

distractors.why: Flourished means thrived, the opposite of going nowhere.
Proliferated means multiplied, which does not fit a single stalled proposal.
Prevailed means succeeded, but the proposal made no progress.

definition: impossible to doubt or dispute because it is so clearly true

examples.text: The photographs provided incontrovertible proof that the glacier had retreated.
The signed order is incontrovertible evidence of who gave the command.
The empty wrapper under his pillow was incontrovertible evidence.

confused.note: Incontrovertible means beyond dispute; controversial means causing much dispute.

questions.passage: For years the company denied that its factory had polluted the river. Then a laboratory matched the chemical in the water to one made nowhere else, evidence so ______ that the firm stopped contesting the charge.
questions.explanation: Evidence that ends all denial cannot be disputed.

distractors.why: Inexplicable means impossible to explain, which does not describe decisive evidence.
Prohibitive means too costly, which does not fit.
Secular means not religious, which does not fit.

partsNote: not able to be turned against

definition: showing a clear and deep understanding of something

examples.text: The essay offers an insightful reading of the novel's final scene.
Her insightful question redirected the whole research program.
My little sister made an insightful comment about why our parents argue over maps.

confused.note: Insightful means perceptive; "inciteful" is not a standard word.

questions.passage: The reviewer praised the biography as unusually ______. Where earlier writers had merely listed the composer's achievements, this author explained why a shy man with no training was driven to write music at all.
questions.explanation: Explaining the deeper reasons behind a life shows real understanding.

distractors.why: Formidable means impressively powerful, which is not what the reviewer highlights.
Harrowing means distressing, which does not fit.
Chronological means in time order; the praise is for depth of understanding.

definition: to bring a feeling, memory, or image into the mind

examples.text: The smell of pine evokes the narrator's childhood winters.
The monument was designed to evoke the grandeur of ancient Rome.
That song evokes the summer I learned to drive.

confused.note: To evoke is to bring a feeling or memory to mind; to invoke is to call on a rule or authority.

questions.passage: The film's opening scene uses no dialogue. Its long shots of empty streets and shuttered windows are meant to ______ a sense of loneliness before a single character has appeared.
questions.explanation: The images are meant to bring a feeling into the viewer's mind.

distractors.why: Invoke means to call upon a law or authority; a feeling is evoked.
Negate means to cancel, the opposite of creating a feeling.
Allocate means to distribute, which does not fit.

definition: to grow or develop successfully

examples.text: The moss flourishes on the shaded northern side of the trees.
Trade flourished along the river for three centuries.
My basil plant is finally flourishing on the sunny windowsill.

confused.note: To flourish is to thrive; to furnish is to supply.

questions.passage: The arts ______ under the new ruler. Within a decade the city had three theaters, a school of painting, and more poets than at any time in its history.
questions.explanation: New theaters, a school, and many poets show the arts thrived.

distractors.why: Languished means weakened or been neglected, the opposite of thriving.
Oscillated means swung back and forth, which does not fit steady growth.
Convened means assembled for a meeting, which does not fit.

definition: to show or declare that something is true

examples.text: Coins found at the site attest to trade with distant ports.
Dozens of studies attest to the drug's safety.
The scratches on the door attest to how much the dog wanted out.

confused.note: To attest is to confirm; to contest is to dispute.

questions.passage: The cave's walls ______ to thousands of years of human presence. Layers of soot from ancient fires cover the ceiling, and handprints in red pigment line a passage deep inside.
questions.explanation: Soot and handprints show that people were there.

distractors.why: Surmise means to guess; the walls provide evidence, they do not guess.
Relish means to enjoy, which does not fit.
Implicate means to show involvement in wrongdoing, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin testis, "witness": to bear witness to

definition: a feeling or idea that a word suggests in addition to its main meaning

examples.text: The poet chose "slender" over "skinny" for its kinder connotation.
The word "empire" carried a proud connotation in 1900 that it has since lost.
"Cheap" and "affordable" mean the same thing but have different connotations.

confused.note: Denotation is a word's literal meaning; connotation is the feeling it carries.

questions.passage: Both "stubborn" and "determined" describe a person who does not give up easily. They differ in ______: the first suggests an unreasonable refusal to listen, the second an admirable strength of will.
questions.explanation: The two words share a core meaning but carry different feelings.

distractors.why: Parity means equality, which does not fit.
Notoriety is fame for something bad, which does not fit.
Aptitude is natural ability, which does not fit.

partsNote: from Latin notare, "to mark": marked along with

definition: a political leader who wins support by stirring up emotions and prejudices, not by reasoned argument

examples.text: The demagogue blamed every hardship on foreigners and promised easy cures.
The play follows a small-town demagogue who talks his neighbors into burning the library.
The debate coach warned us not to argue like demagogues.

confused.note: A demagogue is a leader who inflames a crowd; a pedagogue is a teacher.

questions.passage: The senator was denounced by his colleagues as a ______. His speeches offered no evidence and no plans, they said, only a list of enemies and a promise that anger would be rewarded.
questions.explanation: A politician who offers anger in place of argument inflames emotions to win support.

distractors.why: A benefactor gives help, which is not what his colleagues accused him of.
A predecessor held a position earlier, which does not fit.
A novice is a beginner, which is not the accusation.

definition: friendly, lively, and enjoyable, said of people or occasions

examples.text: The convivial host fills every glass before it is half empty.
Treaties were often settled over long, convivial dinners.
The neighborhood block party was a convivial affair that lasted past midnight.

confused.note: Convivial describes lively, festive company; congenial means pleasant and well suited to you.

questions.passage: Meetings of the historical society are surprisingly ______. Members arrive with homemade cakes, greet one another like old friends, and often linger for an hour after the lecture to trade stories.
questions.explanation: Cakes, warm greetings, and lingering to chat make a friendly, lively occasion.

distractors.why: Harrowing means extremely distressing, the opposite of these meetings.
Secular means not religious, which is not the point.
Prohibitive means too costly, which does not fit.

definition: impossible to explain or understand

examples.text: For reasons that remain inexplicable, the birds abandoned the island in a single season.
An inexplicable sadness settles on the heroine as the train leaves.
My brother has an inexplicable fear of balloons.

confused.note: Inexplicable means impossible to explain; inextricable means impossible to untangle.

questions.passage: Engineers checked every circuit and found nothing wrong. The satellite's sudden silence remained ______ until, three weeks later, it began transmitting again as if nothing had happened.
questions.explanation: A failure with no cause that anyone could find cannot be explained.

distractors.why: Incontrovertible means beyond dispute, which does not describe a mystery.
Contemporary means of the present time, which does not fit.
Adequate means good enough, which does not fit.

definition: belonging to the present time; or living at the same time as someone else

examples.text: The play retells an ancient myth in a contemporary setting.
Contemporary accounts of the battle disagree about who fired first.
The museum has one floor of old masters and one of contemporary art.

confused.note: Contemporary means of the present or of the same time; temporary means lasting a short while.

questions.passage: The historian relies chiefly on ______ sources. She prefers the letters and diaries of people who witnessed the revolution to the memoirs that survivors wrote forty years afterward.
questions.explanation: Letters written by witnesses at the time belong to the same period as the events.

distractors.why: Secular means not religious, which is not the distinction drawn.
Pedestrian means dull and ordinary, which is not the contrast with later memoirs.
Avid means keenly eager, which does not describe sources.

definition: extremely important and necessary

examples.text: Iron is vital to the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
Control of the river was vital to the city's survival.
Sleep is vital the night before a long drive.

confused.note: Vital means essential; a vial is a small bottle.

questions.passage: The mangrove forests play a ______ role along the coast. Their tangled roots hold the shoreline in place, shelter young fish, and absorb the force of storm waves that would otherwise flood the villages behind them.
questions.explanation: Holding the shore, sheltering fish, and blocking waves make the forests essential.

distractors.why: Negligible means too small to matter, the opposite of these functions.
Pedestrian means dull and ordinary, which does not fit.
Prohibitive means too costly, which does not fit.

definition: to keep or continue to have something

examples.text: Clay soils retain water far longer than sandy ones.
The duke retained his title but lost his lands.
I retained almost nothing from the lecture I half slept through.

confused.note: To retain is to keep; to restrain is to hold back from action.

questions.passage: Although the building has been converted into apartments, it ______ many features of the original factory. Residents live among exposed brick walls, iron columns, and windows three meters tall.
questions.explanation: Keeping the brick, columns, and windows is continuing to have original features.

distractors.why: Relinquishes means gives up, the opposite of keeping.
Anticipates means expects, which does not fit.
Convenes means calls together, which does not fit.

definition: using new ideas or methods

examples.text: An innovative design lets the bridge sway safely in high winds.
The city's innovative sewer system became a model for the continent.
My teacher has an innovative way of explaining fractions with pizza.

confused.note: Innovative means new and inventive; innate means inborn.

questions.passage: The school's approach to mathematics is ______. Students do not sit through lectures; they are given a real problem, such as designing a bus timetable, and discover the methods they need along the way.
questions.explanation: Replacing lectures with real problems is a new method.

distractors.why: Pedestrian means dull and ordinary, the opposite of a fresh approach.
Secular means not religious, which is not the point.
Prohibitive means too costly, which does not fit.

definition: enough in amount or good enough in quality for a purpose

examples.text: The sample was adequate for one test but not for two.
The fort's walls were adequate against arrows but not against cannon.
My cooking is adequate: nobody complains, and nobody asks for seconds.

confused.note: Adequate means good enough; inadequate means not enough.

questions.passage: The committee did not call the applicant's essay brilliant. It judged the writing merely ______, clear enough to follow and free of serious errors, but without a single memorable sentence.
questions.explanation: Writing that is clear and correct but unremarkable is good enough and no more.

distractors.why: Innovative means new and inventive, which the committee did not find.
Harrowing means distressing, which does not fit.
Vital means essential, which does not describe mediocre writing.

definition: not connected with religion

examples.text: The new republic replaced church courts with secular ones.
The poet moves from hymns to secular love songs in her later work.
The school holds a secular winter concert with songs about snow.

confused.note: Secular means not religious; sectarian means relating to a particular religious group.

questions.passage: The old cathedral school once taught only scripture and Latin prayers. In the nineteenth century it added ______ subjects, including chemistry, geography, and modern languages.
questions.explanation: Chemistry and geography are subjects not connected with religion.

distractors.why: Hallowed means sacred, the opposite of nonreligious subjects.
Convivial means festive and friendly, which does not describe subjects.
Avid means keenly eager, which does not fit.

definition: a person who held a job or position before someone else; an earlier version of something

examples.text: The new queen reversed nearly every policy of her predecessor.
The telescope is ten times as powerful as its predecessor.
My phone's predecessor lasted five years; this one cracked in a week.

confused.note: A predecessor comes before; a successor comes after.

questions.passage: The new mayor inherited a city deep in debt. Her ______ had borrowed heavily to build a stadium that was used only a dozen times a year.
questions.explanation: The person who held the office before her left the debt.

distractors.why: A benefactor gives help, which is not what the earlier mayor did.
A demagogue inflames crowds; the sentence concerns who held office before her.
A successor comes after, but the borrowing happened before she took office.

definition: to send someone or something to a place for a particular purpose

examples.text: The king dispatched a rider to warn the border forts.
The agency dispatched a team to sample the lake after the spill.
I dispatched my little brother to the kitchen for snacks.

confused.note: To dispatch is to send off; to dispense is to hand out.

questions.passage: Within an hour of the earthquake, the government had ______ rescue teams to the affected region. Helicopters carried doctors and engineers to villages that could no longer be reached by road.
questions.explanation: Sending teams to the region is dispatching them.

distractors.why: Retained means kept, the opposite of sending out.
Anticipated means expected, which does not fit sending teams.
Convened means called together for a meeting, which does not capture sending teams outward.

definition: to expect something and prepare for it

examples.text: Forecasters anticipate a wetter winter than usual.
The general anticipated the attack and moved his cannon overnight.
I did not anticipate how long the line for the roller coaster would be.

confused.note: To anticipate is to expect; to participate is to take part.

questions.passage: The designers of the bridge ______ that traffic would double within twenty years. They therefore built it with four lanes, though two would have been enough on the day it opened.
questions.explanation: Building for future traffic shows they expected the increase and prepared for it.

distractors.why: Dispatched means sent, which does not fit.
Contended means argued; the designers acted on an expectation, which is anticipating.
Reproached means expressed disappointment in someone, which does not fit.

definition: ordinary and dull; lacking imagination

examples.text: Critics found the sequel's plot pedestrian after the brilliance of the original.
The treaty's pedestrian language hides how radical its terms were.
The restaurant's menu is pedestrian: burgers, fries, and a sad salad.

confused.note: Pedestrian means dull and ordinary; plebeian means common or of the lower classes.

questions.passage: The architect's early buildings were daring. His later work is disappointingly ______, a series of plain office blocks that could have been designed by anyone.
questions.explanation: Plain buildings anyone could design are ordinary and unimaginative.

distractors.why: Innovative means inventive, which describes his early work.
Harrowing means distressing, which does not fit.
Vital means essential, which does not fit.

definition: to argue or state that something is true; or to compete or struggle

examples.text: The lawyers contended that the treaty had never been properly signed.
Some researchers contend that the fossil belongs to a new species.
My sister contends that she called the front seat first.

confused.note: To contend is to argue or compete; content means satisfied.

questions.passage: Most scholars date the manuscript to the twelfth century. Professor Ito ______, however, that it is at least two hundred years older, pointing to the style of its handwriting and the recipe for its ink.
questions.explanation: She argues for a different date and offers reasons.

distractors.why: Concedes means admits reluctantly, but she is disputing the usual view.
Speculates means guesses without firm evidence; she supports her claim with specific evidence.
Anticipates means expects, which does not fit arguing about a date.

definition: to win or be successful after a struggle; to be common or usual

examples.text: After a long siege, the defenders prevailed.
Dry conditions prevail across the plateau for most of the year.
Common sense finally prevailed, and we stopped for directions.

confused.note: To prevail is to win out; to avail is to be of use.

questions.passage: For two days the jury was split. In the end the arguments of its most patient member ______, and all twelve agreed that the evidence was too weak to convict.
questions.explanation: The member's arguments won out after a struggle.

distractors.why: Languished means weakened and was neglected, the opposite of winning out.
Convened means assembled, which does not fit arguments.
Speculated means guessed, which does not fit.

definition: very eager and enthusiastic

examples.text: An avid reader, the heroine has finished the village library by twelve.
The emperor was an avid collector of clocks.
My grandfather is an avid gardener who talks to his tomatoes.

confused.note: Avid means eager; arid means very dry.

questions.passage: The retired pilot is an ______ birdwatcher. She rises before dawn most mornings, has recorded more than nine hundred species, and once flew to another continent to see a single rare owl.
questions.explanation: Rising early and traveling far for one bird show great eagerness.

distractors.why: Apathetic means lacking interest, the opposite of her enthusiasm.
Secular means not religious, which does not fit.
Pedestrian means dull, which does not describe her devotion.

definition: to guess about something without having enough facts to be certain

examples.text: Astronomers speculate that the moon's ice came from comets.
Historians can only speculate about why the city was abandoned.
We speculated about who the new teacher would be.

confused.note: To speculate is to guess; to stipulate is to demand as a condition.

questions.passage: No letters from the painter's final year survive. Biographers can only ______ about why she abandoned the nearly finished mural and never returned to it.
questions.explanation: Without evidence, biographers can only guess.

distractors.why: Attest means to confirm with evidence, which they lack.
Contend means to argue a definite claim; "only" and the lack of letters call for guessing.
Dispatch means to send, which does not fit.

definition: the state of being equal, especially in pay, status, or power

examples.text: The treaty gave the two navies parity in the number of warships.
The two methods reached parity in accuracy after the software update.
The players demanded parity in prize money between the two tournaments.

confused.note: Parity is equality; a parody is a comic imitation.

questions.passage: For decades, nurses at the city's two hospitals were paid at different rates for identical work. The union's chief demand was ______: the same wage for the same job, wherever it was performed.
questions.explanation: The same wage for the same job is equality.

distractors.why: A disparity is an inequality, which is what the union opposed.
Notoriety is fame for something bad, which does not fit.
A connotation is an implied meaning, which does not fit.

definition: the state of being famous for something bad

examples.text: The pirate's notoriety spread to every port on the coast.
The duel brings the young poet a notoriety he does not want.
My brother gained brief notoriety for setting off the fire alarm with burnt toast.

confused.note: Notoriety is fame for something bad; notability is the quality of being worthy of notice.

questions.passage: The chemist had hoped to be remembered for his research. He achieved ______ instead, as the man whose careless experiment burned down the university's oldest building.
questions.explanation: Being known for a destructive mistake is fame for something bad.

distractors.why: Parity is equality, which does not fit.
Acclaim is praise, the opposite of the reputation he earned.
Aptitude is natural ability, which does not fit.

definition: extremely upsetting or frightening

examples.text: The survivor's harrowing account of the shipwreck fills three chapters.
Refugees told harrowing stories of the march across the mountains.
The drive home through the ice storm was harrowing.

confused.note: Harrowing means deeply distressing; hallowed means sacred.

questions.passage: The climbers' descent was ______. Caught by a storm near the summit, they spent two nights without shelter, lost their only rope in an avalanche, and reached the base camp with frostbitten hands.
questions.explanation: Nights exposed to a storm, an avalanche, and frostbite are deeply frightening.

distractors.why: Convivial means cheerful and festive, the opposite of this ordeal.
Pedestrian means dull and ordinary, which this descent was not.
Adequate means good enough, which does not fit.

definition: to come together or bring people together for a meeting

examples.text: The king convened a council of nobles to decide on war.
The society convenes every spring to share new research.
We convened at the kitchen table to plan the surprise party.

confused.note: To convene is to assemble; a convent is a community of nuns.

questions.passage: When the river rose to within a meter of the levee, the mayor ______ an emergency meeting of the town's engineers. They gathered at midnight in the fire station and worked until dawn.
questions.explanation: Calling the engineers together for a meeting is convening it.

distractors.why: Dispatched means sent away, the opposite of bringing people together.
Rescinded means cancelled, but this meeting was just being called.
Retained means kept, which does not fit.

definition: so high or severe that it prevents people from buying or doing something

examples.text: Prohibitive tariffs ended the import of foreign cloth.
The prohibitive cost of the treatment limits it to a few hospitals.
The price of concert tickets was prohibitive, so we watched the stream.

confused.note: Prohibitive means too costly or severe to allow; prohibited means forbidden.

questions.passage: Engineers agree that a tunnel under the strait is technically possible. The obstacle is its ______ cost: at an estimated forty billion dollars, it would exceed the two countries' combined transport budgets for a decade.
questions.explanation: A cost exceeding a decade of budgets is high enough to prevent the project.

distractors.why: Adequate means sufficient, which does not describe an obstacle.
Negligible means too small to matter, the opposite of forty billion dollars.
Contemporary means of the present time, which does not fit.

definition: to express disappointment in or disapproval of someone's actions

examples.text: She reproaches herself for the letter she never answered.
The queen reproached her generals for their caution.
My mother reproached me for forgetting my grandmother's birthday.

confused.note: To reproach is to express disapproval; to approach is to come near.

questions.passage: The coach did not shout at the goalkeeper who had let in the winning shot. She did, however, quietly ______ him for having skipped practice twice that week.
questions.explanation: Quietly expressing disapproval of skipped practices is reproaching him.

distractors.why: Dispatch means to send, which does not fit.
Anticipate means to expect, which does not fit.
Vilify means to slander harshly, far too strong for a quiet word of disapproval.

partsNote: from Latin prope, "near": to bring near, to bring up against

definition: having unlimited power

examples.text: The emperor was treated as omnipotent, though his generals made every decision.
The novel's narrator is omnipotent, moving characters like chess pieces.
To a toddler, whoever holds the cookie jar seems omnipotent.

confused.note: Omnipotent means all-powerful; omniscient means all-knowing.

questions.passage: The company's founder appeared ______ to those who worked for her. She could hire or dismiss anyone without explanation, and no decision, however small, was final until she had approved it.
questions.explanation: Controlling every hiring and decision makes her seem to have unlimited power.

distractors.why: Omniscient means all-knowing; the details describe unlimited power.
Avid means eager, which does not fit.
Inexplicable means impossible to explain, which does not describe her authority.
